ordered_diagnoses: Autosomal Dominant Nocturnal Frontal Lobe Epilepsy

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and altered mental status with focal neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Episodes of prominent dizziness, vertigo, and intermittent left arm shaking
Bouts of dull response with partial awareness
Recurrent episodes lasting about 5 minutes, occurring more than 10 times a day
key_facts: 67-year-old male with hypertension and coronary artery disease
Presented with episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and left arm shaking
Episodes occurred while playing Mah-Jong
Partially aware of what was happening but unable to think during episodes
Each episode lasted about 5 minutes
Episodes recurred more than 10 times a day
No prior history of seizures
Blood pressure was 200/110 mmHg at triage
Neurological examination was unremarkable except for dull response during events
No focal brainstem signs, left-right disorientation, dyslexia, dysgraphia, or finger agnosia
Basic laboratory data were within normal limits
Brain MRI revealed non-specific white matter changes
EEG showed rhythmic epileptiform discharges originating from the right frontal area
